epic.title: EPIC-26: Export (Excel, PowerPoint, PDF)
epic.functionalNeed:
Stakeholders need to take an analysis out of the product: into a slide deck for a presentation, a flat document for offline sharing, and a spreadsheet for their own exploration. This epic delivers three exports that all draw from the same live analysis data, so the numbers always agree with the dashboard.
The PowerPoint deck mirrors the dashboard for the current snapshot and the selected markets, AI engines and categories. It opens with a cover that carries the brand, the snapshot date, the scope and an AI-generated In-Brief summary, then walks through identity, performance and sources at the overall level, and repeats a focused section for each category. Every chart is built from native, editable shapes (not screenshots), so a user can adjust any text after export. The PDF is the same deck flattened to a fixed-layout document for offline sharing. The Excel workbook is the data backbone: an Overview tab, a tab for the corporate-reputation pillars, one tab per category, and a Raw Data tab with one row per question and engine for downstream tooling.
Each export is bounded so a single slide or sheet stays readable: rankings and source lists are capped at the top entries, the share-of-voice chart groups the long tail into "Others", and the brand-territory view shows the strongest topics. The full totals are still surfaced (for example, the source slide states how many domains and citations the top ten were drawn from), so nothing silently disappears. Where a view shows everything (the prioritization matrix plots every category or brand per market, with overlapping points grouped into clusters that are listed in full in a side panel), that is intentional.
---

> As a user, I want to export my analysis as a branded PowerPoint deck, so that I can present the findings to stakeholders.
scope: > As a user, I want every export to reflect the snapshot and scope I am viewing, so that the shared artifact matches the dashboard.
- Given a selected snapshot and a market and engine selection, When I export to any format, Then the deck, PDF and workbook reflect that snapshot and selection.
- Given the analysis covers multiple categories, When I export, Then each category gets its own deck section and its own workbook tab.
- Given a metric or list is capped on a slide or sheet, When I review it, Then the full total is still stated somewhere on that view so nothing is silently dropped.

stories.title: User Story 11.4: Scope and snapshot fidelity
stories.userStory:
As a **user**, I want every export to reflect the snapshot and scope I am currently viewing, so that the shared artifact matches exactly what I see on my dashboard and nothing is silently dropped.

---
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1 — Snapshot + scope fidelity**

- **Given** I have selected a specific snapshot and a combination of markets and AI engines, **When** I export to any format (PPTX, PDF, or Excel), **Then** the deck, PDF, and workbook reflect that snapshot and those active LLM + country/language filters.

**AC2 — LLM and country filters respected**

- **Given** I am viewing the dashboard filtered to 2 of 4 available markets and 3 of 5 available AI engines, **When** I export to any format, **Then** the exported artifact contains only data for those 2 markets and 3 engines — not all markets or all engines.

**AC3 — Categories: PPTX/PDF always full**

- **Given** the analysis covers multiple categories, **When** I export to PPTX or PDF from any page (Overview or a category page), **Then** the deck always contains the full report: overview section + one 4-slide section per category, in the same order as the dashboard.

**AC4 — Categories: Excel always full**

- **Given** the analysis covers multiple categories, **When** I export to Excel from any page, **Then** the workbook always contains the full report: Overview tab + Brand Pillars tab + one tab per category + Raw Data tab.

**AC5 — No silent drops**

- **Given** a metric or list is capped on a slide or sheet (e.g. top 10 brands, top 10 domains), **When** I review it, **Then** the full total is still stated on that view (e.g. "Top 10 of 47 domains") so nothing is silently dropped.

**AC6 — Export always covers full report**

- **Given** the export is triggered from any page (Overview or a category page), **When** the export runs, **Then** the exported artifact always covers the **full report** (overview + all categories) — the active LLM filters and country/language filters are applied, but the content is never scoped to a single category. _(PM clarification, 2026-06-21)_

---

stories.title: User Story 11.3: Excel workbook export
stories.userStory:
As a **user**, I want to export my analysis as an Excel workbook, so that I can explore the underlying data, build my own views, and use the raw LLM responses for downstream analysis.

---
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1 — Workbook structure (5 tabs)**

- **Given** an analysis with results, **When** I export to Excel, **Then** I receive a workbook with these sheets:

| Sheet | Contents | Cap|
| Overview | Identity (In-Brief, corporate reputation, brand territory, top concepts), Performance (KPI metrics, category prioritization, brand rankings), Sources (media-type split, top domains) | Brand rankings top 10|
| Brand Pillars | 4 dimensions (Brand Image, Employer Brand, ESG/Sustainability, Leadership) x engine; each row: dimension, engine, sentiment, insights, Source URLs (pipe-separated), Source Domains (pipe-separated) | 4 dimensions|
| One tab per category | Same spine as Overview, scoped to that category | Brand rankings top 10|
| Raw Data | One row per question x engine: snapshot, country, category, type, question, engine, favorability, sentiment, themes, full response (type-aware), Source URLs (pipe-separated), Source Domains (pipe-separated) | Ranking text capped at top 10 entries|

**AC2 — Type-aware Raw Data responses**

- **Given** the Raw Data sheet, **When** I open it, **Then** visibility questions show no prose answer; competitive answers carry comparison prose + winner + ranking; perception answers carry the full free text.

**AC3 — Pipe-separated sources**

- **Given** the source columns in Raw Data, **When** I load the workbook into spreadsheet tooling, **Then** Source URLs and Source Domains are pipe-separated so they can be split into rows for analysis.

**AC4 — Ranking format in Raw Data**

- **Given** a visibility or competitive row, **When** I read the ranking, **Then** it is formatted as "1. Brand (chosen) — 2. Brand * — 3. Brand …" where * marks the target brand and "(chosen)" marks the engine's top pick.

**AC5 — XLS UX flows**

Three alternative flows are designed. Engineering must benchmark real export size and generation time, then implement the matching flow(s):

- **Flow A — Fast / Low Volume:** "Your export has started. It will be ready soon" toast → completion toast with "Download Export" + email copy. No modals.
- **Flow B — High Volume (volume > cap):** "Export spreadsheet?" modal warns about cap. Actions: Cancel / Export anyway. Completion toast restates the cap.
- **Flow C — Slow Export:** Started toast → "We'll email your export" modal → email delivery + optional inline completion toast if user is still on the page.

Copy corrections vs Figma mock (annotation card 06):

- "Your expert has completed" → "Your export has completed"
- "Domaines" → "domains"

---

stories.title: User Story 11.2: PDF export
stories.userStory:
As a **user**, I want to export my analysis as a PDF, so that I can share a flat, offline document that anyone can open without PowerPoint.

---
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1 — Export trigger & flow**

- **Given** an analysis with results, **When** I click the export icon button in the toolbar and select "PDF", **Then** a "Your export has started" toast appears immediately and the download begins.
- **Given** the PDF download is ready, **When** it completes, **Then** a "Your export has completed" success toast appears with a "Download Export" action.
- **Given** the export fails, **When** the failure is detected, **Then** an error toast appears with a "Try again" action and no broken file is downloaded.

**AC2 — Same content as PPTX, fixed layout**

- **Given** the PowerPoint deck (Story 11.1), **When** I export to PDF, **Then** I receive the same slides flattened to a fixed-layout document with identical content and ordering.
- **Given** the PDF is generated, **When** I open it, **Then** every slide from the PPTX deck is present (cover + 7 overview slides + 4 slides per category) in the same order, with the same footer on all content slides.

---

stories.title: User Story 11.1: PowerPoint deck export
stories.userStory:
As a **user**, I want to export my analysis as a branded PowerPoint deck, so that I can present the findings to stakeholders with an editable, native-shapes presentation.

---
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1 — Export trigger & flow**

- **Given** an analysis with results, **When** I click the export icon button in the dashboard toolbar and select "Presentation .pptx", **Then** a "Your export has started" toast appears immediately and the download begins.
- **Given** the PPTX download is ready, **When** it completes, **Then** a "Your export has completed" success toast appears with a "Download Export" action.
- **Given** the export fails, **When** the failure is detected, **Then** an error toast appears with a "Try again" action and no broken file is downloaded.

**AC2 — Native editable shapes**

- **Given** any chart in the deck, **When** I open it in PowerPoint, **Then** every text element is editable because all charts and visuals are built from native shapes — not images or screenshots.

**AC3 — Footer**

- **Given** the deck is generated, **When** I review any content slide, **Then** it carries a consistent footer: "Onclusive – GEO AI Analysis" on the left, "{Brand} AI Visibility Report – {slide number}" on the right. The cover slide has no footer.

**AC4 — 8 overview slides**

- **Given** the deck is generated, **When** I open it, **Then** the overview section contains exactly these 8 slides:

| Slide | Contents | Cap|
| Cover | Brand name + logo, snapshot date, scope (markets/engines/categories), InBrief lockup "powered by AI Sense" | Summary trimmed to fitting bullets|
| How AI perceives your brand | Corporate reputation: 4 dimensions (Brand Image, Employer Brand, ESG/Sustainability, Leadership) with sentiment + insights | 4 dimensions, up to 3 insights each|
| What your brand is known for | Brand-territory topics as proportional bubbles | Top 8 topics|
| The concepts shaping how you're seen | Concepts by frequency with sentiment + source counts (two columns) | Top 10 concepts|
| How your brand performs across AI engines | 4 KPI cards (Visibility, Avg Position, LLM Choice, Sentiment) + SOV-by-engine donut below; target brand's SOV always shown in donut centre | 4 metrics; donut = top brands + "Others" tail|
| Category performance matrix | Visibility x LLM Choice quadrants (50%/50%), one flag marker per category x market; overlapping markers collapse into lettered cluster bubbles with full-membership panel | All categories + markets plotted; clusters listed in full|
| How you rank against competitors | Brand ranking by visibility; no SOV column | Top 10 brands|
| Which sources shape your AI presence | Media-type split + domains with favorability; subtitle states full domain + citation totals | Top 10 domains|

**AC5 — Per-category sections**

- **Given** the analysis covers categories, **When** I open the deck, **Then** each category adds its own 4-slide section: (a) KPI cards + SOV-by-engine donut, (b) brand prioritization matrix (your brand vs competitors on Visibility x LLM Choice), (c) top 10 concepts, (d) top 10 of N sources.

**AC6 — Export button availability**

- The export button is present on both the Overview page and each Category page.
- Regardless of which page the export is triggered from, the exported deck always covers the **full report** (overview + all categories) — only the active LLM filters and country/language filters are applied. The export is never scoped to a single category. _(PM clarification, 2026-06-21)_
